==Problem==

How many different combinations of <imath>\$5</imath> bills and <imath>\$2</imath> bills can be used to make a total of <imath>\$17</imath>? Order does not matter in this problem.

<imath>\textbf {(A)}\ 2 \qquad \textbf {(B)}\ 3 \qquad \textbf {(C)}\ 4 \qquad \textbf {(D)}\ 5 \qquad \textbf {(E)}\ 6</imath>

==Solution==

Since four <imath>\$5</imath> bills total to <imath>\$20</imath>, at most three <imath>\$5</imath> bills may be used.

If three <imath>\$5</imath> bills are used, the <imath>\$2</imath> bills must total to <imath>\$2</imath>, so one <imath>\$2</imath> bill may be used.

If two <imath>\$5</imath> bills are used, the <imath>\$2</imath> bills must total to <imath>\$7</imath>, which is impossible since <imath>7</imath> is odd.

If one <imath>\$5</imath> bill is used, the <imath>\$2</imath> bills must total to <imath>\$12</imath>, so six <imath>\$2</imath> bills may be used.

If no <imath>\$5</imath> bills are used, the <imath>\$2</imath> bills must total to <imath>\$17</imath>, which is impossible since <imath>17</imath> is odd.

Thus there are <imath>\boxed {\textbf{(A)}\ 2}</imath> such combinations of bills that total to <imath>\$17</imath>.
